issues.description: Resolver.resolve() postcondition silently weakened: returned requirements may no longer be fully prepared.
issues.detail: The deleted loop in resolver.py previously guaranteed every returned requirement had prepared=True and needs_more_preparation=False. That obligation is now shifted to each caller without documentation or assertion. Third-party consumers and future commands relying on the old contract will silently break. State the new postcondition in a docstring on resolve() and/or assert it.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist introduces a fourth dist source with implicit precedence and no documented invariants.
issues.detail: get_dist now prefers _distribution over metadata_directory over local_file_path with no comment explaining why a cached metadata-only dist wins. After prepare_linked_requirements_more fully downloads the wheel, the cached metadata-only dist still shadows the real one. Either invalidate _distribution on full prep or document the precedence; add docstring stating preconditions.

issues.description: download_info backfill in _fetch_metadata_only mixes concerns and rests on undocumented preconditions.
issues.detail: _fetch_metadata_only now synthesizes download_info via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) guarded by 'if download_info is None'. req.source_dir may be unset in metadata-only mode, and the contract for the resulting DirectUrl is unstated. pip lock / --report consumers may receive subtly different hashes/archive_info than the full-download path.

issues.description: prepare_linked_requirements_more call site duplicated across three command modules instead of composed once.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each independently invoke preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more after resolve(). Three copies of the postcondition-restoration ritual invite drift and increase the chance the next command forgets it. Extract a small helper or restore the call to the resolver behind a dry-run flag.

issues.description: No test proves --dry-run actually avoids the wheel download for PEP 658 metadata cases.
issues.detail: The load-bearing behavioral claim is that dry-run no longer fetches the full wheel when PEP 658 metadata exists. The diff contains no integration test (e.g., a mock index that fails on wheel GET) pinning that property. Without such a test, a future refactor silently re-introduces the download.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the change moves in the right direction — defer full preparation out of the resolver so --dry-run avoids unnecessary wheel downloads when PEP 658 metadata exists — but objects to how it was done. Resolver.resolve()'s postcondition was silently weakened and the obligation pushed onto callers without docstring, assertion, or contract update. InstallRequirement gained a mutable dist cache (set_dist/get_dist) with a four-way precedence ladder and no stated invariants, risking a stale metadata-only dist shadowing a fully prepared one. The download_info backfill inside _fetch_metadata_only entangles two concerns and rests on undocumented preconditions about req.source_dir. Fix: write the contracts down, invalidate or document _distribution precedence, consolidate the duplicated prepare_linked_requirements_more call, and add a test asserting no wheel is fetched under --dry-run.
